title: A Career in Whisky Sales | Craft Beer School
desc: What whisky sales jobs in India involve: retail and bar visits, state routes to market, schemes, numbers and the product knowledge that helps.
teaser: Whisky sales in India runs state by state, shop by shop. The people who do well know the product as well as the numbers.
standfirst: Sales is the largest commercial career path in the whisky industry. In India it is shaped by state excise rules, government wholesale corporations in some states and strict limits on advertising. Here is what the job involves and what helps people succeed in it.
sections:
A field sales executive looks after a territory of retail shops, bars, restaurants and hotels. The job is to make sure the company's brands are listed, in stock, visible and correctly priced. That means regular outlet visits, checking stock, talking to owners and staff and following up on orders through the distributor or the state system.

Above field roles sit area managers, key account managers for hotel chains and modern retail. State heads sit above them. Each level manages people and numbers, but the work still starts with knowing what happens in each outlet.
Every state is a different job

Alcohol is a state subject in India. Some states sell through government wholesale corporations, others through licensed private distributors and a few through state-run retail. Each state sets its own excise, approves prices and labels and controls how stock moves. A few states have prohibition.

That makes whisky sales in one state very different from the next. In a corporation state the company sells to the corporation and works hard on retail visibility. In a distributor state, managing the distributor relationship is central. Rules change, so salespeople learn the current system in their state from the company's compliance team.

Sales teams work with nine-litre cases, the standard spirits unit equal to twelve 750 ml bottles. Targets are usually set in cases by brand and pack. Indian portfolios include 750 ml, 375 ml and 180 ml packs. The smaller packs often move the most volume in economy price bands.

Other numbers matter too: numeric distribution (how many outlets stock the brand), stock cover in the trade, shipments against depletions and price band mix. Our guide to building a whisky sales dashboard explains how those numbers fit together.

Direct advertising of alcohol is restricted in India. That puts more weight on the sales team. Visibility in the shop, staff knowledge in bars and trade relationships do much of the work that advertising does in other categories.

Product knowledge becomes a real advantage. A salesperson who can explain the difference between a blended whisky and a single malt, or why a sherry cask finish tastes different, earns trust from bar managers. Training bar staff to serve and describe whisky responsibly is part of many sales roles.
The festive calendar sets the pace

Sales peak from Diwali through the wedding season to New Year. Gifting drives premium brands and gift packs. Dry days, such as Gandhi Jayanti in most states and election days, close sales. Sales teams plan visits, stock and promotions around this calendar.

The rhythm is intense in the last quarter of the calendar year and quieter in the monsoon. People who enjoy pace and targets usually thrive. Those who prefer steady, predictable work may find the peaks hard.

Selling alcohol carries responsibility. Sales teams follow the age rules of each state. They never promote heavy drinking. At trade events and tastings, measures are small, water is on hand and nobody drives after drinking. Many companies have strict codes on what sales staff can offer outlets, so knowing the policy protects both you and the company.

A typical field day starts with a plan of fifteen to twenty outlet visits in a set route. At each shop the salesperson checks which SKUs are on the shelf, how many cases are in the back, whether prices match the approved MRP and whether the brand is placed where customers see it. Bars and restaurants need a different conversation: which whiskies are on the back bar, how staff describe them and what sells by the peg.

Notes from each visit go into a sales app or report. The evening is often spent on follow-ups with the distributor or depot about pending orders. Managers review the numbers weekly against target. It is a job with a lot of travel and a lot of repetition. The people who stand out build real relationships with outlet owners over years, which no scheme can replace.
How to get in and grow

Many whisky salespeople start in fast-moving consumer goods sales and move across. Graduates with an MBA or a commerce degree join as management trainees. Hospitality professionals with bar experience bring product knowledge that companies value.

A practical first step: learn how whisky is made, from grain to cask, so you can talk about the product with confidence. Our guide to how whisky is made is a good start. Then visit a few shops and bars as a customer and notice which brands are visible and why.
faqs: Do I need a background in alcohol to work in whisky sales?
No. Many people come from FMCG or hospitality sales. Product knowledge can be learned and helps a lot.
Why is whisky sales different in each Indian state?
Each state controls excise, prices, labels and routes to market, so the sales model changes from state to state.
